Now don't get me wrong, I think nvidia overpriced from the start due to a lack of competition, and we need AMD to be competitive. comments.text:
As I said on Steve, Brett, and Kyle's programs regarding the 5600 XT: This is Navi to the 056th Power, this card after the VBIOS update to make its performance on par with that of Vega to the 064th is exactly what this card needed to be from the get~go, not the more energy~efficient Vega 056 successor that would be available for what the Reference Card goes for now (actually, Vega to the 056th goes for a few tens of dollars less than 5600 XT now, if you look hard enough in the New market; its Vega 064 that's a disaster, and at least Radeon VII is now between 0479.99 and 0529.99$ USD before taxes), this is ideal First Generation Vega Quality Gaming from Navi at a price that honestly makes for a great GTX 1060 (06 GB) successor.
That said though, be forewarned: Even if you upgrade this card to Vega 064 performance or better, Workstation performance will still be shot because of Navi 056 having only a 06 GB option, rather than an 08 GB option, so while you may be able to do some streaming and specific video production workloads, you will not be able to do everything right off the bat, especially since we're in a scenario where Sony/MAGIX Vegas Pro does not officially support Generation 0I Navi on Versions 0I to 0I6, with Version 0I7 getting it in one of its next major updates (unless it's already happened; Rob Williams of Techgage will give us an RX 5000 follow~up article when that time comes); ultimately, Gen 0I Navi is for Gaming, Gen II Navi will definitely be the Vega Workstation successor, so if you are a media producer that wants to upgrade from your Vega to the 064th or Radeon VII and you rely heavily on OpenCL, wait for Generation II Navi, wait for the RadeoNII (Radeon Eleven/Radeon Pro Navi II; official names pending), Gen 0I was good to set the bar for what is ideal Super HD (I080p) performance but we need something for the high tier so that Vega II can finally have a proper successor, even though I'll stick with my Radeon VII with the Ryzen 3950X for at least 2020 to 2027.

AMD Cards are known to have driver issues so be warned if you buy one. [I have an AMD card before you call me an NVIDIA shill]
From FPS drops, to freezing/crashing or no startup at ALL from well optimized games.Hell,when I was using my RX 5700 XT from Gigabyte in December, I could barely watch YouTube or use Discord without blackouts from my monitor anytime a video/gif appeared
The updates have helped but they still have issues
1.Turn off settings Enhanced Sync and Image Sharpening in Radeon Software can help
2.The fan settings on the AMD cards seem to prioritize quiet over cooling and like to default back when you start you PC again. So remember to check  your fan settings.


NVIDIA cards although maybe more expensive, they are much more stable/compatible like with OpenGL applications, AMD not so much...Just putting this out so others can make more informed decisions because I only see people saying this on review pages from vendors [Newegg/Amazon etc] aside from myself

I believe that they can do it if RDNA 2 is finally running with the new instruction set. 
VEGA(GCN) and RDNA 1(GCN) are quite similar but RDNA 2 is build from the ground up. 
Probably less compute heavy and more specialised like nvidia chips are resulting in less unused chip area. GCN leaves (in gaming workloads) much of the transistors without a task but they still need to be powered ( that's one reason for the higher power draw ).
If you lookup how small the NAVI 10 chip is compared to nvidias offerings ( i know that nvidia is still on 14nm but even compensating for that ) RDNA 1 is a huge step in performance per area and this makes me hopeful.
